property_summary: After any sequence of calls to Put, the balance of each user must equal the total ETH they have ever sent to Put, but the mutant overwrites the balance causing it to only reflect the last msg.value.
After a user makes two successive Put calls, the user's Acc[user].balance in the reference equals the sum of the two msg.values, while in the mutant it equals only the second msg.value.

After any number of Put calls, a user's Acc.balance must equal the total msg.value they sent across all their Put transactions; the mutant overwrites balance, so it only reflects the last msg.value, and a subsequent Put call reduces or strips previous contributions.

Reference: For any user, after any sequence of Put calls, the user's Acc.balance must equal the sum of all msg.values they sent via Put. Mutant: It breaks because after multiple Put calls, Acc.balance reflects only the last msg.value, violating the invariant that balance tracks cumulative deposits.

After any call to Put, the sender's balance in Acc must be at least the total msg.value they have ever sent in Put calls; the bug never adds msg.value, so a Put call with msg.value > 0 leaves balance unchanged and breaks this invariant.
After a Put call, the sender's Acc balance must be at least the msg.value sent; the bug never adds msg.value, so a Put with msg.value > 0 leaves balance unchanged and violates this.
After a successful Put call, the sender's Acc balance must be strictly greater than before; the bug keeps balance unchanged, violating this.

After a successful Put call with msg.value > 0, the sum of Acc[msg.sender].balance plus msg.value must be greater than the balance before the call; the bug never adds msg.value, so the balance remains unchanged and this invariant is violated.
After a Put call, the sender's Acc balance must be at least msg.value; the bug never adds msg.value, so a Put with msg.value > 0 leaves balance unchanged and violates this.
The sum of all Acc balances plus the contract's own Ether balance should equal total Ether ever deposited; the bug breaks this by not adding msg.value to acc.balance on Put.
After a Put call, a user's recorded balance in Acc should strictly equal the amount they sent; the bug breaks this by not incrementing acc.balance.
After a call to Put, the acc.balance of msg.sender must increase by the exact msg.value sent; the bug breaks this by not incrementing acc.balance.

After a Put call, the change in the contract's Ether balance must equal the change in the caller's Acc balance plus any Ether sent via the call; the bug fails to increase acc.balance so the equality breaks.
For any address that calls Put with Ether, the caller's recorded balance must increase by at least the Ether sent, but the bug never records the increase, so the balance doesn't grow.
After calling Put, the unlockTime must always be greater than or equal to the block.timestamp at the time of the call; the bug allows setting unlockTime to a past timestamp, violating this invariant.

For any address that has called Put, the unlockTime recorded in Acc must never be less than the block.timestamp of the Put transaction; the mutant allows unlockTime to be set to an earlier timestamp, so a subsequent Collect call with a timestamp between the recorded unlockTime and the real Put timestamp will succeed in the mutant but fail in the reference.

For any address that calls Put, after the call the unlockTime recorded in Acc must be greater than or equal to the block.timestamp at the time of the Put call; the mutant allows unlockTime to be strictly less, violating this invariant.

For any address and any unlock time, after a Put call the recorded unlockTime must be >= block.timestamp of the Put. The mutant allows _unlockTime < block.timestamp, enabling Collect to succeed despite the block time not exceeding Put's timestamp.

After any Put call, the recorded unlockTime must be >= the block.timestamp at the time of the Put, ensuring Collect cannot succeed before that timestamp. The bug allows unlockTime to be set arbitrarily early, letting an adversary call Collect before the Put's block.timestamp and steal funds.

For any user with a pending unlock, after Put is called with a future _unlockTime, the unlock time should be set to at least that provided _unlockTime; the buggy version ignores it and sets unlockTime to the current block.timestamp, so unlockTime < _unlockTime when _unlockTime is strictly in the future.

After Put is called with a strictly future _unlockTime, the user's unlockTime must be strictly greater than block.timestamp at the time of the call; the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, so it's not strictly greater.

For any caller and any strictly future _unlockTime, after Put(...) the caller's unlockTime must be at least the provided _unlockTime; the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After any call to Put with a strictly future _unlockTime, the caller's unlockTime must equal the provided _unlockTime; the buggy version sets it to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

After Put with any _unlockTime, the caller’s unlockTime must be >= the maximum of _unlockTime and block.timestamp at the time of the call; the mutant sets it to block.timestamp, violating this when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.
After any call to Put, the LogFile history length must increase by exactly one; the bug deletes the LogFile.AddMessage call so the history length does not increase.
After any call to Put, the LastMsg in LogFile must record the latest Put parameters; the bug omits the AddMessage call so LastMsg is not updated.
After a call to Put, the History array length of the Log contract referenced by LogFile must increase by exactly 1; the buggy version omits the AddMessage call, so the length does not increase.
After any call to Put, the LogFile's History array length must be strictly greater than its length before the call; the bug omits AddMessage, so the length stays the same.
After a successful Put, the LogFile's History length must be greater than before the call; the buggy version omits LogFile.AddMessage, so the length stays the same.
A Collect that succeeds must happen strictly after acc.unlockTime, not at or before it.
If Collect does not revert, timestamp must be strictly greater than unlockTime, never equal.
A successful Collect must occur only when the block timestamp is strictly greater than the unlock time.
If Collect succeeds (does not revert), block.timestamp must be strictly greater than unlock.

property_summary: If a Collect call succeeds, the contract balance must have decreased by exactly the collected amount; the bug allows collection exactly at unlockTime, violating the invariant that funds are locked until after unlockTime.
After any successful Collect, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block.timestamp; the mutant allows Collect when block.timestamp equals unlockTime.

If a Collect succeeds, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block.timestamp; the buggy >= condition allows collection when block.timestamp equals unlockTime, violating the time-lock invariant.

For any successful Collect call, the caller's unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block.timestamp; the buggy >= condition allows collection when block.timestamp equals unlockTime, breaking the time-lock invariant.

After a Collect call does not revert, the caller's Acc.unlockTime must be strictly less than the current block.timestamp; the buggy >= condition allows a successful Collect when block.timestamp equals unlockTime, breaking the time-lock requirement.

property_summary: A successful Collect call implies that the caller's balance before the call was at least MinSum.
After a successful Collect, the caller's balance in Acc must remain at least MinSum if MinSum was previously required, but the bug allows Collect to reduce the balance below MinSum.

After any call to Collect(uint256 amt), the caller's Acc balance must never be less than MinSum (1 ether) if the original if-condition would have prevented the collection, but the mutant allows collection leaving balance below MinSum.
After any call to Collect, if the caller's Acc.balance is less than MinSum, the call must have reverted, but the mutant allows a successful Collect that leaves balance below MinSum.

After any call to Collect(uint256 amt), if amt > 0 and block.timestamp > acc.unlockTime and the call does NOT revert, then either acc.balance BEFORE the call was >= MinSum or the contract's Ether balance did not change; the bug allows a successful Collect when acc.balance < MinSum, which reduces the contract's Ether balance without the MinSum guard.
